text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a sustained cluster of very large continuous batches from tenant-A during the 09:00 window. latency p95 spiked to ~420ms even though overall GPU utilization was fine. looks like a single tenant kept winning the coalesce window and growing the batch shape.

megan: Interesting. Any logs/metrics? is it prefix-heavy traffic or lots of short responses concatenated?

alex: Quick summary: request size distribution shifted right (avg tokens/request ~ 900 -> 1.6k). coalesce window still 20ms. a few long-running streams kept getting appended to the same batch, growing token count until we hit our max-steps. log snippet: `batch_id=0x7f9 tokens=12800 tenants=[A:124, B:12] p95=420ms`

rishi: That matches what I saw in the trace. tenant affinity + continuous-batching means one tenant can dominate if its tail latency allows it to stay in-window. Proposed short-term: add a soft per-tenant live-token quota and a cheap admission check to cap per-tenant contribution to a coalesce group.

sam: Soft quota makes sense, but we need to be careful about fairness vs throughput. If we cap tenant-A it'll push more batches overall (more small batches) which could increase per-token cost. tradeoff is explicit.

kai: Two knobs worth discussing: (1) per-tenant live-token cap to limit runaway shaping, (2) aggressive lane separation for tenants with high average tokens (move to a dedicated microqueue). both are orthogonal. per-tenant cap is low-friction; lane separation is heavier but isolates tail behavior.

alex: Prototype config I'd try:
```
batcher.coalesce_window_ms = 20
batcher.max_batch_tokens = 16384
batcher.per_tenant_max_live_tokens = 4096  # soft, leaky-bucket style
```
If tenant hits soft cap, it gets minor admission delay (~1-2 coalesce windows) not full preempt.

megan: Can we implement soft cap as a credit ledger instead of hard queue moves? that way we can do decay and burst allowance. also helpful for telemetry.

rishi: Yep — credit ledger + decay window (e.g., 5s) would let tenants burst then be throttled if sustained. Implementation note: ledger updates must be atomic in the admission path; we can piggyback on the envelope that computes request.size_tokens.

ops-bot: :warning: Alert triggered: high-coalesce-batch-variance detected on node gpu-14, 09:04:22 -> 09:12:01. annotation: tenant-A contributed 78% of tokens in top-10 batches.

sam: @alex @rishi if we go ledger route, let's ensure the scheduler exposes a diagnostic endpoint showing per-tenant live tokens and historical decay curve. ops folks will need that.

kai: Also consider a fallback: when per-tenant shaping repeatedly triggers, escalate to lane separation automatically (configurable threshold e.g., >60% tokens for 2m). that avoids manual interventions.

alex: Agreed. Two-stage plan: 1) ship soft credit ledger (low-risk) + telemetry 2) evaluate automated lane separation policy.

megan: Can someone open a follow-up RFC? include microbench guidance: measure p50/p95/p99, per-token cost delta, and e2e request tailgen with synthetic tenant patterns.

sam: I'll prototype the ledger and a lightweight telemetry endpoint. will do a canary on dev cluster. @kai can you sketch the lane separation API (queue creation + re-route rules)?

kai: Will do. rough sketch: `POST /scheduler/v1/queues` with selector `{tenant: string, min_avg_tokens: int}` and `PUT /scheduler/v1/routes/{tenant}` for temporary reassignment. keep re-route idempotent.

rishi: One implementation caveat: moving inflight KV cache ownership during lane separation is tricky. we should prefer new requests routed to new lane and let inflight finish in old lane to avoid cache churn. mark as TODO in RFC.

alex: Perfect. Action items: sam -> ledger prototype, kai -> queue API sketch, megan -> RFC template + perf checklist, rishi -> admission atomicity notes. I'll create the thread ticket and tag ops. :thumbsup:

megan: Thanks everyone — documenting findings in the RFC will help avoid repeating this.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Created incident-followup ticket INF-7234 linked to this thread.
